name: BindableEvent
simple: A BindableEvent lets scripts on the SAME side talk to each other: server Script to server Script, or LocalScript to LocalScript. One script fires it, and every script listening runs its function. It does not cross between server and players; that is what RemoteEvents are for.
analogy: A BindableEvent is like a school bell inside one building. When someone rings it, every classroom in that building hears it. A building across the street (the other side of the client-server boundary) hears nothing.
whenToUse: One server Script needs to tell other server Scripts something happened, like 'round over'.
Making your own custom event, like a `Died` or `LevelUp` event for your own system.
Not for server-to-client messages. Use a RemoteEvent for that.
where: Create it in Studio or with `Instance.new("BindableEvent")`. Put it where your scripts can find it, like ServerStorage (server-only) or ReplicatedStorage.

terms.server: The one computer, run by Roblox in a data center, that is in charge of a game. Every player in the same game is connected to it. It keeps the official copy of the game, like who has how many coins.
terms.client: Your own device (phone, PC, Xbox) running the game. Every player has their own client. The client draws the screen and reads your keyboard, mouse or touch.
terms.client-server boundary: The invisible wall between the server and each client. They are different computers, so a script on one side cannot just reach over and change a variable on the other side. Messages have to be sent across.
terms.fire: To send off an event so that the functions listening to it run.
terms.event / signal: Something that can happen, like `PlayerAdded` or `OnServerEvent`. You connect a function to it and that function runs each time it happens.
terms.connect: Telling Roblox: when this event happens, run my function. You do it with `:Connect(function() ... end)`.
terms.same side: Both scripts run on the server, or both run on the same player's client.

examples.title: Tell other server scripts the round ended
examples.place: Two Scripts in ServerScriptService, BindableEvent named RoundEnded in ServerStorage
examples.code:
-- Script A: the round timer
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
local roundEnded = ServerStorage:WaitForChild("RoundEnded")

task.wait(60)
roundEnded:Fire("Red team") -- tell everyone listening

-- Script B: gives out rewards
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
local roundEnded = ServerStorage:WaitForChild("RoundEnded")

roundEnded.Event:Connect(function(winner)
	print(winner .. " won! Giving rewards...")
end)
explain: Script A calls `Fire` with the winner's name.
Script B was listening with `.Event:Connect`, so its function runs and receives the same value.
Both scripts are on the server, so a BindableEvent is the right tool.

gotchas: It does not cross the client-server boundary. A LocalScript firing it will not reach a server Script.
Values are copied, not shared: if you fire a table, listeners get a copy, and functions or metatables inside it are lost.
Make sure the listener connects before you fire, or it will miss the message.

BindableEvent:Fire.simple: Rings the bell. Every function connected to `.Event` runs, with the values you pass.
BindableEvent:Fire.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local levelUp = Instance.new("BindableEvent")

levelUp.Event:Connect(function(newLevel)
	print("Reached level", newLevel)
end)

levelUp:Fire(5) --> Reached level 5

BindableEvent.Event.simple: The event that runs each time someone calls `Fire` on this BindableEvent. Connect a function to it to listen.
BindableEvent.Event.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
local roundEnded = ServerStorage:WaitForChild("RoundEnded")

roundEnded.Event:Connect(function(winner)
	print("Winner:", winner)
end)
